label: Crafted Sounds
description: Life on the Lawn is a Philadelphia band's plodding, guitar-forward indie rock record, with the loping, anxious 'Wasting the Weekends' as a standout. The songs move at a deliberate, slowcore-adjacent pace, wrapped around conversational, downcast lyrics. It sits closer to the scene's slacker and power-pop wing than to overt country, but the tempo and mood put it near the Core's quieter side.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Pavement-descended slacker rock, with a slowcore undertow that recalls the hushed-twang lane.
borderline_note: Tags read as indie rock/power pop rather than overt twang; included on the strength of its slowcore pacing and press description, a judgment call between C7 and C8.

label: cooked raw
description: This self-titled debut is a spare, home-recorded set of guitar rock from Philadelphia's A Country Western. The songs are short and plainly played, favoring direct, diary-like lyrics over polish. It's for listeners who like their slacker rock small, quiet, and unvarnished.
lineage: A DIY, pandemic-era continuation of the Bandcamp slacker-rock tradition that the band would later sharpen on Life on the Lawn.

label: Self-released
description: Spent is a ten-song set of plainspoken, guitar-driven folk-rock from St. John's songwriter Andrew Smith, tagged by the artist himself as folk and alt-country. The songs are built from long, narrative verses about touring, fading friendships, and small-town memory, sung in a conversational near-talk-sing delivery. It's for listeners who like wordy, unhurried songwriting with a small-town eye.
lineage: Continues the plainspoken, guitar-and-voice songwriting line that runs from '90s alt-country through 2010s Bandcamp singer-songwriters.

label: Self-released
description: Glutton For Punishment is Kansas City band Big Fat Cow's fuzzed-out country-rock record, self-tagged 'fuzz folk' and 'post rock' alongside 'country' and 'folk'. A song called 'Goodbye Gram Parsons' makes the band's cosmic-country reference points explicit, while the rest of the record piles distorted guitar onto loose, rootsy song structures. It's for listeners who want their twang loud and ragged.
lineage: The song 'Goodbye Gram Parsons' names a direct reference point; the fuzz-over-country sound resembles 2010s-2020s loud indie-twang bands.

label: Self-released
description: A five-song follow-up EP that opens with 'Yellow Belly Boy' and keeps Big Fat Cow's fuzzy, country-tagged guitar rock intact in a shorter format. The band again tags itself 'fuzz folk' and 'post rock' alongside straight 'country,' and the songs keep the loose, rowdy energy of their full-length in a tighter run of tracks.
lineage: A shorter continuation of the band's cosmic-country/fuzz-folk sound established on Glutton For Punishment.

label: Self-released
description: Good Grief is Birmingham, Alabama band Bitter Calm's debut full-length, self-tagged 'chamber rock' and 'slowcore.' The eight songs move at a hushed, unhurried pace with sparse arrangements built around clean guitar and restrained vocals, matching the band's own description of itself as 'big big sad.' It is the quieter, earlier half of the band's Core-era catalog.
lineage: Sits in the Low/Duster-descended slowcore-and-sadcore line, rendered by a young indie band rather than a '90s one.

album: Eternity In The Lake of Fire
label: Self-released
description: Eternity In The Lake of Fire is Bitter Calm's nine-song second record, again tagged 'chamber rock', 'indie rock', and 'slowcore' on the band's own page. The band's notes frame it around self-annihilation and hopelessness, and the arrangements add violin, bass, and percussion to the hushed guitar-and-voice core. 'Sinner' is the clearest way in.
lineage: Extends the slowcore, sadness-as-method tradition into a darker, more full-band-oriented record than the debut.

label: Self-released
description: There Will Be Chicken Wings is a twelve-song Raleigh, North Carolina record self-tagged 'southern rock', 'alt country', 'countrycore', and 'countrygaze' on Bandcamp. It moves between rowdy, full-band roots rock and slower, heavier passages, with plainspoken lyrics about small-town Southern life. It's for fans of loud, wall-of-guitar country in the Wednesday mold.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the Wednesday-style template of loud, distorted guitars under country song structure.

label: Self-released
description: Sunfall is an Austin songwriter's ten-track home-recorded record, self-tagged 'americana,' 'california country,' and 'psychedelic folk.' The songs are warm and unhurried, built on acoustic fingerpicking and drifting, sun-bleached melodies rather than twang or fiddle. It plays like a bedroom-scale entry in the Laurel Canyon-descended cosmic-country revival.
lineage: Channels the breezy, Gram Parsons/Laurel Canyon-descended cosmic-country sound through a solo, DIY bedroom recording.

label: Self-released
description: A seven-song companion EP from the same year as Sunfall, tagged with the same 'americana', 'folk-psych', and 'psychedelic' terms. It keeps the same hazy, acoustic-led sound in a shorter run of songs such as 'Naturally' and 'Winds'. It's for listeners who liked Sunfall and want more of its sun-bleached drift.
lineage: A shorter, same-year sibling to Sunfall in Buckley Willis's cosmic-country/psych-folk catalog.

label: Gar Hole Records
description: Famous Lunch is New Orleans songwriter Chris Acker's ten-song full-length, tagged 'alt country', 'americana', and 'country folk' by the artist. Backed by a band with pedal steel, Acker sings plainspoken, funny-then-heartbreaking narrative songs with a loose, live-sounding feel. 'Wouldn't Do For You (Buddy)' is one of the record's centerpieces.
lineage: Sounds indebted to the Prine/Townes line of plainspoken storytelling, filtered through a New Orleans dancehall-country band.

label: Gar Hole Records
description: Odd, Ordinary, & Otherwise is Chris Acker's thirteen-song full-length, again tagged 'alt country', 'americana', and 'country folk'. The Bandcamp notes say it ranges from quiet, introspective tunes to barn burners, written partly during 2020 isolation. It shows the same plainspoken, detail-heavy songwriting that runs through his catalog.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Prine-style storytelling; an earlier stage of the songwriting heard on Famous Lunch.

label: Self-released
description: Slow Country is a twelve-song record from Chicago's Conor Lynch, self-tagged 'folk rock', 'indie rock', and 'singer-songwriter' with a self-described 'mid-fi' aesthetic. Song titles like 'Steam Whistle' and 'Long Ways From Home' point to the record's rural, travel-worn imagery, set over loose, unpolished guitar arrangements. It's for listeners who like home-recorded folk-rock with rough edges left in.
lineage: A lo-fi, home-recorded take on folk-rock storytelling in the Bandcamp singer-songwriter tradition.

label: Self-released
description: Cooper Kenward's self-titled twelve-song debut is tagged 'alternative', 'folk', and 'singer-songwriter' by the Los Angeles artist. The songs favor plain, conversational lyrics over polish, in the vein of the barroom and bedroom-folk wing of the Core scene. It's a DIY-scale starting point for listeners who later found 'Dying in a Diner'.
lineage: Early, DIY-scale entry in the same LA singer-songwriter lane later refined on Dying in a Diner.

label: Soggy Anvil Records
description: Dying in a Diner is Cooper Kenward's ten-song Soggy Anvil Records release, still tagged 'alternative', 'folk', and 'singer-songwriter'. The artist's notes frame the record around memory, like paging through old photos, with songs that range from loose and unguarded to slow-built. 'Orbit' and 'Over Easy' are good ways in.
lineage: Continues the plainspoken LA singer-songwriter thread of his self-titled debut; sounds akin to MJ Lenderman-adjacent conversational songwriting.

label: Self-released
description: Always The Moon is a nine-song Pensacola, Florida record self-tagged 'folk', 'country', and 'indie'. The songs are guitar-and-voice driven, with plainspoken, downcast titles ('Father Time', 'Treading Water', 'Sycophant To Sorrow') typical of the singer-songwriter side of the scene. It's for listeners who like small, sad country-folk songs.
lineage: A small-scale, self-released entry in the plainspoken new-country/singer-songwriter lane.

label: Self-released
description: sending is a six-song EP from Harrisonburg, Virginia band Dogwood Tales. It includes an early version of 'mt jackson', a song about a family member's hospitalization that the band would later re-record for a full-length. The EP's tone is plainspoken and small-town-focused, consistent with the rest of the band's catalog.
lineage: An early sketch of songs the band would develop further on Every Star in Rockingham County.

label: WarHen Records
description: Rodeo is a six-song vinyl EP played by a full band of acoustic and electric guitar, bass, pedal steel, and drums. It is a straightforward alt-country record built on real pedal steel and full-band arrangements rather than fuzz or distortion. It's for listeners who want the band's most traditionally country side.
lineage: Represents the more traditionally country-instrumented side of Dogwood Tales' catalog, released through the same regional vinyl label as 13 Summers 13 Falls.

label: WarHen Records
description: 13 Summers 13 Falls is a five-song vinyl EP released the same year as Rodeo through WarHen Records. It keeps the band's plainspoken, small-town songwriting in a shorter, quieter set than its companion release, with songs like 'Hard To Be Anywhere' and 'Since Yesterday'.
lineage: A same-year, same-label companion to Rodeo in Dogwood Tales' developing alt-country catalog.

label: Born Losers Records
description: Every Star in Rockingham County is Dogwood Tales' twelve-song Born Losers Records full-length. The label copy describes pedal steel chords, delicate harmonies, and power-pop drumming set against lyrics about small-town Shenandoah Valley life, hospital bills, and pop-culture touchstones like Princess Peach and McDonald's. It re-records 'Mt. Jackson', first heard on the EP 'sending', as its emotional centerpiece.
lineage: Its label copy places it in a Townes Van Zandt-descended songwriting tradition; musically it sounds akin to current lo-fi indie country.

label: Self-released
description: Fat, Evil Children's self-titled six-song EP is tagged 'americana,' 'indie folk,' and 'indie rock' by the Los Angeles band. It includes 'Weedpuller,' the playlist's entry point, alongside plainspoken, mid-tempo songs that lean folk and Americana rather than punk or fuzz despite the band's name.
lineage: A small-scale LA entry in the 2010s-2020s Bandcamp Americana/indie-folk lane.

label: Self-released
description: Can't Stop is Fat, Evil Children's second six-song EP, tagged with the addition of 'emo' alongside the band's usual 'americana' and 'indie folk' tags. The songs keep the same plainspoken, mid-tempo approach as the debut EP, with slightly more emotionally direct, anthemic moments.
lineage: A continuation of the band's Americana/indie-folk sound with a newly added emo edge, connecting it to the scene's emo-twang crossover wing.

label: Meritorio Records
description: swan is the second full-length from New Zealand project Fazed on a Pony, tagged 'alt-country', 'emo', and 'indie rock'. The label copy says it expands from the project's earlier Pavement-esque indie rock into arrangements with pedal steel, fiddle, drum machines, and synths, and compares it to MJ Lenderman, David Berman, and Sparklehorse. 'Heart Goes Blank' is the clearest way in.
lineage: Its label copy compares it to MJ Lenderman, David Berman, and Sparklehorse; it sounds indebted to that line of wry, twangy indie songwriting.

label: Self-released
description: it'll all work out is Fazed on a Pony's earlier eight-song full-length, tagged 'alt-country,' 'emo,' and 'indie rock' like its follow-up. It represents the more straightforwardly 'Pavement-esque' indie-rock sound that swan's own liner notes say the project later expanded outward from.
lineage: The earlier, leaner version of the alt-country/indie-rock songwriting Fazed on a Pony built out further on swan.

note: Third album per Americana UK review (Soggy Anvil Records); contains 'Wheelies', the playlist track. Not found on cooperkenward.bandcamp.com at time of research, so tracklist/exact date/label could not be independently confirmed from a scraped page.
